label: DM2 + HTN follow-up
transcript:
Dr. Lee: Good to see you again, Mr. Alvarez. How have you been since your last visit?
Patient: Honestly, my sugars have been running high in the mornings, 180 to 210. I've been thirsty a lot and getting up at night to urinate.
Dr. Lee: Are you taking metformin 1000 mg twice a day as prescribed?
Patient: Yes, every day. I did miss lisinopril a couple of times last week.
Dr. Lee: Your blood pressure today is 148 over 92, heart rate 84. A1c from last week came back at 8.9%. Weight is up three pounds. Let's start you on empagliflozin 10 mg daily and increase lisinopril to 20 mg daily. I also want a basic metabolic panel and a urine microalbumin today. Please follow up in 6 weeks and we'll recheck A1c in 3 months. Let's also refer you to nutrition for a diabetes diet review.
Patient: Okay, sounds good.

structured_input.chief_complaint: Elevated home glucose readings and nocturia

label: CHF exacerbation follow-up
transcript:
Dr. Patel: Mrs. Chen, you were hospitalized last week for heart failure. How are you breathing today?
Patient: Still short of breath climbing stairs, and my ankles are swollen by evening. I gained four pounds since discharge.
Dr. Patel: Blood pressure 128/78, heart rate 96, oxygen 94% on room air. Lungs with bibasilar crackles, 2+ pitting edema. Your BNP was 820 at discharge. I'm going to increase torsemide from 20 to 40 mg daily and add spironolactone 25 mg daily. Continue carvedilol and sacubitril-valsartan. Please do daily weights and call if you gain more than 2 pounds in a day. I'll order a BMP and an echocardiogram, and refer you to the heart failure clinic. Follow up with me in 2 weeks.
Patient: Understood, thank you.

structured_input.chief_complaint: Dyspnea on exertion and lower extremity edema post-CHF admission
